answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can give each identity a reputation score that decays over time unless the agent keeps doing useful, verified work. One pearl of good work is not enough to let an agent wander through the system unchecked; the score only stays high with steady contributions. A fresh identity starts at zero, so an attacker must spend weeks of real effort to grow each walnut-sized credential into something trusted, and abandoning a burned identity means starting over. The cost of many fakes becomes the cost of many long, honest histories.
